subject: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@carebridge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. We captured your PHI handling patterns and the constraints that matter for CareBridge's triage workflow.

Summary from today
- Use case: Real-time symptom triage + extraction of structured fields (diagnosis codes, medication mentions). Outputs will feed your EHR ingestion pipeline.
- PHI surface: patient name, DOB, free-text notes, sometimes images (we only discussed text for now).
- Compliance requirements: BAA required; SOC 2 Type II report requested for vendor security posture; data residency in US.

Questions we called out for qualification
1) Is there an internal requirement to prevent any cleartext PHI leaving your VPC (i.e., must all inference occur inside a customer-managed environment)?
2) Do you need persistent storage of inference artifacts (logs / traces) retained longer than 30 days?
3) Any MFT or SFTP procurement constraints we should loop procurement on now?

Proposed deployment eligibility options (high-level)
- Hosted (Redwood API) + redaction layer: Fastest, suitable if CareBridge accepts Redwood-managed inference but requires agreement on redaction and a BAA. We can offer token-level redaction and automatic key-stripper for known PHI attributes.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): Customer-dedicated capacity in our cloud region; data logically isolated; best balance of throughput and control.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): Full customer-managed network and KMS/HSM; required if your policy prohibits external inference endpoints.

Immediate next steps / asks from CareBridge
- Please return the completed vendor security questionnaire (attached) by EOD next Wed (2027-09-08) so our security team can triage.
- Confirm whether inference must be customer-local (VPC/on-prem) or if Dedicated/Hosted are acceptable with a BAA.
- If SOC 2 Type II is the bar, let us know whether you need the report itself or just a SOC 2 assertion letter and custom attestations.

Attachments: vendor questionnaire attached (PDF) — feel free to answer inline.

I'll loop in Marissa for SOC 2 sharing logistics and Rishi for deployment eligibility once we hear back.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: carebridge_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)]
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@carebridge.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Desai <rajiv.desai@carebridge.ai>, procurement <procurement@carebridge.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 19:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- For high-volume triage, we would prefer not to run everything in-prem; Dedicated or Hosted is acceptable if the BAA and data handling controls satisfy our legal. Our security team leans toward Dedicated for predictability.
- We do need to retain inference logs for 90 days for auditability, but those can be stored in an encrypted bucket — retention policy is negotiable.
- SOC 2: we require the Type II report, but we can accept a secure view/shared copy (not public).

We'll start filling out the questionnaire this week and aim to return by 2027-09-07. Procurement will review cost anchors once you provide an initial dedicated-capacity pricing sketch.

Emily
Emily Turner
Head of Product, CareBridge
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@carebridge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Emily. Notes and follow-ups below: 

1) Retention: 90-day logs is fine — we'll note that as a requirement for the deployment scoping doc.

2) SOC 2 Type II access: Marissa, can you confirm how we can share the report under an NDA and the expected turnaround?

3) Pricing: Aditya — can you assemble a high-level Dedicated capacity ballpark (monthly) + delta for Private VPC? Procurement wants numbers to compare.

4) Redaction / PHI handling: To avoid false positives we typically recommend a two-layer approach — client-side redaction for PII, plus server-side token filtering for known PHI attributes. If CareBridge accepts Dedicated, we can additionally offer a private KMS so keys never leave your control.

Attached the SOC sharing instructions text (link + process) to make the procurement/ssecurity review easier.

Thanks — will keep this thread as the record.

Naomi

[Attachment: redwood_soc2_sharing_instructions.txt]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Turner <emily.turner@carebridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 12:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan

Naomi / team — quick security notes so Emily has clarity from our side: 

- SOC 2 Type II: We can provide a secure, time-limited view of the report via our compliance portal once an NDA is signed. Typical turnaround to provision is 48 business hours after NDA.
- Evidence: For onboarding we can supply architecture diagrams, encryption-at-rest proofs, key management design, and sample audit logs (sanitized). We cannot provide raw customer logs.
- BAA: Redwood executes a standard BAA for customers handling PHI; legal can start a draft once CareBridge confirms they want Hosted/Dedicated and signs an NDA.
- PHI routing: If CareBridge requires that inference occur inside customer network, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended path. For Dedicated we offer private subnets and optional egress controls; however, Dedicated still traverses our managed infra in the chosen cloud region (we'll document the exact network boundaries).

I'll prepare a short checklist (1 page) with the exact artifacts procurement/security will ask for — will share in this thread by EOD Fri.

Marissa
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Turner <emily.turner@carebridge.ai>, Rajiv Desai <rajiv.desai@carebridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HIPAA requirements walkthrough + deployment options — action plan

Quick technical note from infra/solutions: 

- Deployment feasibility based on your stated needs (real-time triage, 90-day logs, SOC2 access): all three modes are viable. Recommendation: start POC on Dedicated to validate latency and throughput; if policy requires full network isolation, move to Private for production.
- For the POC we will:
  * Provide a sandbox Dedicated pool pinned to a model family (you can choose quantized variant).
  * Enable KMS-backed encryption for logs with customer-provided keys optional.
  * Expose an ingestion endpoint that can accept either redacted text or tokenized payloads — we can test both to compare extraction accuracy.

Next steps (assignment):
- CareBridge: return the vendor questionnaire by 2027-09-07.
- Redwood (Aditya): draft Dedicated capacity estimate and a POC SOW by 2027-09-06.
- Redwood (Marissa): SOC2 portal NDA + 1-page procurement checklist by 2027-09-03 EOD.

I'll join the kickoff POC call once procurement signs off.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
